Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Household, washing & chores

burn verb

set fire to; hurt with heat

also burn up, burn down, set fire to, set on fire, burn yourself, burnt, catch fire, put out a fire

classical

Plaut. Most. 609a: ūrit male
Verg. A. 7.13: ūrit odōrātam nocturna in lūmina cedrum (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 284

ūrō, ūrere, ussī, ustum

verb, third conjugation

The general verb: to burn something, and of fire, heat or the sun, to burn or scorch someone. Short u in ustum, as the lexicon writes adustus for now.

Other words

  • incendō, incendere, incendī, incēnsum — set fire to, set alight

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 1.5.2: oppida sua omnia … incendunt (Lewis & Short); Traupman 376

  • cremō, cremāre, cremāvī, cremātum — burn up, burn to ashes

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 84: cujus ā mē corpus est cremātum (Lewis & Short); Traupman 284

    Of things burnt to nothing, books, rubbish, a city; above all of burning the dead.

Examples

  • calidum hoc est: etsī procul abest, ūrit male.

    this is hot: even from a distance it burns badly.Plaut. Most. 609a

  • Cavē nē digitōs ūrās.

    Mind you don’t burn your fingers.composed

  • ignem concipere

    to catch fireTraupman 315

  • admōtō ignī ignem concipere

    to catch fire when a flame is put to itCic. de Or. 2.190 (Lewis & Short s.v. ignis)

  • incendium exstinguere

    to put out a fireTraupman 315

See also fire, burn, burn, kindle a fire, hot.
